newsitem.title: DENMARK: Rieber mulls next Phoenix move.
newsitem.headline: Rieber mulls next Phoenix move.

text.p: Norway's Rieber and Son said on Wednesday it was studying the possibility of raising its bid for Phoenix Contractors after the Danish roadbuilder hinted that Rieber was its preferred suitor.
"We are conducting a series of evaluations and analyses. This process will continue for a while now," Rieber's managing director Olav Daviknaes told Reuters.
Phoenix on Tuesday said it was unable to completely recommend any of three takeover bids it received, but indicated that a new Rieber offer would be favourably viewed.

In its statement the Phoenix board pointed to the Rieber bid as being best for the company's continued autonomy and future development but said the Norwegian firm's cash offer, the lowest of three so far, was insufficient.
Daviknaes said that a new offer for Phoenix was on the agenda at a Rieber management meeting to be held in its Bergen headquarters later on Wednesday.
"We are aware that Phoenix in its statement presented us with an open invitation to make a fresh bid. But we have not decided yet what we are going to do," Daviknaes said.
Danish construction and chemicals group Superfos A/S offered last Thursday to pay 700 crowns per share for Phoenix A-shares, and 620 crowns for the most-traded C-share.
The offer trumped an earlier bid by Rieber but was later outdone by small provincial Danish building contractor Marius Pedersen which offered 710 crowns per A-share and 625 crowns per C-share.
Phoenix has summoned shareholders to an extraordinary meeting in Vejen, its west Denmark base, on February 21, prior to making its final recommendation.
